newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - catch-up expected on Monday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - catch-up expected on Monday.

text.p: U.S. muni cash prices remained flat throughout the little-noticed Friday session, but market players said they were hopeful prices would catch up with Treasury gains once the market gets back to business Monday.
"Good things are going to happen on Monday," one trader said, citing the full point gain enjoyed Friday by the U.S. Treasury long bond, which was yielding 6.36 percent for the first time since March.
The trader said munis failed to keep pace strictly because virtually no one was around to make a trade.
"If I had to quote it higher, maybe we're 1/8 higher, but I didn't have a trade," he said.

The new issue calendar is set to rebound sharply next week, as scheduled competitive and negotiated sales are expected to total $3.9 billion in 153 offerings for the week, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $1.7 billion in 105 issues. The largest issue is a $320 million Los Angeles Harbor Department deal on Wednesday.
Negotiated sales total $2.2 billion in 48 offerings for the week. One of the largest is expected to be a $210 million Florida Ports Commission deal through senior manager Merrill Lynch & Co.
